A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoseFuse3D-KI framework and CHKI-Video dataset. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite added evaluations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original interpolation experiments on CHKI-Video and FCVG-Test-HC, component ablations, and qualitative results, including Tables 1–6 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds temporal-gap experiments, quantitative interpolation without ground-truth controls, a user study and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The visual encoders, SMPL-X joint/vertex aggregation, condition fusion, Wan2.1 adaptation and training objective remain unchanged. The linear SMPL-X interpolation pipeline used in the new quantitative evaluation already appears in v1 Section 7.4.

E1.justification: CHKI-Video and the 54-clip FCVG-Test-HC benchmark are retained. V2 adds targeted coverage of longer temporal gaps and qualitative corner cases, including virtual animation and robotics videos (Section 5.3 and Figure 8). Interpolation without ground-truth controls was already demonstrated qualitatively in v1.

E2.justification: The original CHKI-Video and FCVG-Test-HC comparator sets remain unchanged. V2 adds FCVG to the previously qualitative in-the-wild evaluation (Table 4). Its new preference and runtime comparisons use subsets of existing baselines: GIMM-VFI, GI and FCVG.

E3.justification: V2 adds several evaluation protocols: 24/48/64/96-frame gaps; quantitative CHKI-Video evaluation with ground-truth controls withheld; preference judgments from 40 participants on 20 scenarios; and timing 25-frame interpolation at 1024 × 576 on the same 80 GB GPU. The original training settings, benchmark protocols and metric descriptions remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds temporal-gap sensitivity testing, quantitative validation of the existing in-the-wild pipeline, perceptual preference analysis, runtime analysis and qualitative robustness cases (Tables 3, 4, 7 and 10; Figure 8). These substantially broaden the questions investigated about practical performance.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars. The user-study participant count describes its evaluation sample, not repeated model runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Every PSNRbbox and PSNRmask entry in the six retained tables increases by 4.77 dB; for example, Table 2's PoseFuse3D-KI values change from 14.72/13.47 to 19.49/18.24. Other retained metrics and rankings remain unchanged, and the revision is unexplained. New results include temporal-gap degradation, annotation-free PSNR of 19.30 versus FCVG's 18.47, 86.50% user preference, and runtime of 212 seconds versus GI's 975 and FCVG's 523. These do not establish a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The CHKI formulation, SMPL-X projection equations, attention definitions and flow-matching objective in Equations 1–6 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the 3D-informed interpolation framework, CHKI-Video dataset and superior benchmark performance. The headline 9% PSNR improvement and 38% LPIPS reduction are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added tests as evidence of long-range robustness, effectiveness without ground-truth controls, broader applicability and runtime efficiency. Existing limitations concerning SMPL-X estimation, generative priors, memory, human-object interactions and linear motion interpolation are retained.

D1.justification: The runtime experiment adds hardware-memory and input-size information. The new checklist states that code and data were unavailable at submission and planned for future release. Existing optimizer, learning rate, LoRA settings, four-GPU FSDP implementation and project link are retained; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to MiraData, HumanVid and Dataset versus Reality, supporting a brief explanation of task-specific dataset curation in Section 7.2. The main related-work positioning remains unchanged. Pexels moves from a footnote to a reference entry rather than becoming a new data source.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the scientific narrative are retained. Changes include small language edits, corresponding-author and conference information, acknowledgements, an expanded dataset rationale, new experimental subsections and a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displayed evidence with tables for temporal gaps, interpolation without ground-truth controls, user preferences and runtime, plus a five-scenario corner-case figure. Existing Figures 1–7 are retained, while original tables are renumbered and some displays relocated. Numerical revisions alone are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful additional evidence about practical interpolation without ground-truth controls, temporal sensitivity, perceived quality and runtime, extending v1's benchmark results and qualitative demonstrations. The net improvement is limited by unexplained PSNR revisions and incomplete reporting: notably, the new checklist denies human-subject research despite Section 7.6's 40-participant study. The added evidence strengthens the paper, but these inconsistencies limit confidence in a larger quality gain.
